description: Proposed garden office within site curtilage detached from main dwelling. Programme including office space, kitchenette and bathroom.
subdivision_of_building: New detached outbuilding within site curtilage
decision_conditions: <p>The outbuilding shall be used solely as ancillary residential space to the host dwelling.</p><p>REASON: In the interests of residential amenity.</p>

<p>The Development hereby permitted shall only be carried out and completed strictly in accordance with the submitted plans hereby approved and any subsequent approval of details.
</p><p>REASON: To ensure that the development hereby permitted is carried out in full accordance with the plans hereby approved.</p>

<div style="">A scheme for the provision and implementation of flood resilient and resistant construction details and measures for the site against surface water flood risk shall be submitted to and agreed, in writing with the LPA in consultation with the LLFA prior to the construction of the measures. The scheme shall be carried out in its entirety before the outbuilding is occupied and; constructed and completed in accordance with the approved plans in line with current best practices.&nbsp;</div><div style="">REASON: To ensure that the development will provide a sustainable drainage system. The condition is required to be discharged prior to the commencement of development to ensure that sustainable drainage is incorporated into the design of the development.</div>

<div style="">Prior to commencement of works, full details and specifications of the green roofs shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The submission shall include the following:<br><ul style=""><li style="margin-left: 15px;">Detailed drawings of a roof plan identifying where the green roofs will be located and the measurement of their coverage; this should include other structures on the roof including location of PV panels, roof lights and access points where applicable, and their relationship with the green roof;</li><li style="margin-left: 15px;">The design of the green roof should be in line with GRO’s code of best practice;</li><li style="margin-left: 15px;">Section drawings demonstrating a minimum substrate depth of no less than 100mm for extensive living roofs;</li><li style="margin-left: 15px;">Details of the drainage system for the roof;</li><li style="margin-left: 15px;">Details of the planting mix, including a minimum of 16+ species for wildflower/extensive roof;</li><li style="margin-left: 15px;">Management and maintenance plan, including access arrangements, irrigation, and general maintenance actions.</li></ul>Within a month of the first occupation of the development, evidence must be submitted to and approved by the Local Planning Authority that the green roof(s) has been delivered in line with the approved details unless otherwise agreed in writing. The green roof shall be retained thereafter for the lifetime of the development in accordance with the approved management and maintenance plan.<br></div><div style="">REASON: To promote biodiversity on site through green roofs, in line with Hackney's Local Plan LP33, policy LP46.</div>

<p><span style="color: rgb(34, 34, 34); font-family: Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif; font-size: small;">The outbuilding's foundation and sub-structure within the Root Protection Area (RPA) of the retained trees shall be implemented in strict accordance with the following requirements:</span></p><ul><li><span style="color: rgb(34, 34, 34); font-family: Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif; font-size: small;">Foundation Type: The foundation for the outbuilding shall be constructed with hand tools only, using screw piles. No mechanical excavation, traditional strip foundations, continuous beams, or trenching may be used within the RPAs of retained trees.</span></li><li><span style="color: rgb(34, 34, 34); font-family: Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif; font-size: small;">Gaseous Exchange: The finished sub-structure must be a suspended ground floor/slab creating a ventilated air space between the underside of the structure and the existing soil surface. This ensures gaseous exchange - the free exchange of air and gases (oxygen and carbon dioxide) between the soil and the atmosphere to maintain a healthy rooting environment.</span></li><li><span style="color: rgb(34, 34, 34); font-family: Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif; font-size: small;">Soil Hydrology: The design must encourage the natural movement and infiltration of rainfall into the soil beneath the structure.</span></li></ul><p>REASON: To safeguard the long-term health, stability, and viability of the retained tree(s) by minimizing soil disturbance in accordance with the principles of BS 5837:2012 "Trees in relation to design, demolition and construction – Recommendations", to accord with the requirements of Section 197(a) of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 and in the interests of visual amenity, having regard to Policy LP51 in the Local Plan 2033 (adopted 2020)</p>

<p>A scheme for the protection of the retained trees in accordance with BS 5837:2012 'Trees in relation to design, demolition and construction – Recommendations' shall be submitted to the Local Planning Authority. This will include a detailed survey indicating the precise position, location, height, canopy spread and Root Protection Area (RPA) of any tree within 7.5m of the application site boundary, together with an Arboricultural Method Statement (AMS) and Tree Protection Plan (TPP) demonstrating how these trees will be protected during the construction process and how their future welfare will not be unreasonably prejudiced by the development. The development shall not commence until any such details are approved by the Local Planning Authority and shall only be carried out in accordance therewith.<br style=""><br style="">REASON: In order to preserve existing trees during building operations and site works pursuant to S.197 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990, and having regard to Policy LP51 in the Local Plan 2033 (adopted 2020).</p>

<p>All new underground utility apparatus, including drainage, shall be routed and installed outside the Root Protection Area(s) (RPAs) shown on the approved drawings. Should it not be feasible to route new underground utility apparatus outside the RPAs of retained trees, trenchless insertion methods (as detailed in BS 5837:2012, Table 3) shall be employed for their installation within the RPAs, with entry and retrieval pits sited outside the RPAs. No other new underground utilities shall be installed within the RPAs of retained trees without prior written consent from the Local Planning Authority (LPA). Any such works, if permitted, shall be carried out in strict accordance with the principles of BS 5837:2012 "Trees in relation to design, demolition and construction – Recommendations" and the National Joint Utilities Group Guidelines for the planning, installation and maintenance of utility apparatus in proximity to trees, Volume 4, Issue 2 (2007) (or any standard that reproduces or replaces this standard).<br style=""><br style="">REASON: To safeguard existing tree(s) in the interests of visual amenity and long-term tree health, having regard to Policy LP51 in the Local Plan 2033 (adopted 2020). Prior approval is required to ensure that important trees are not permanently damaged or lost due to root disturbance or changes in soil hydrology.</p>
